name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text:
**Decision:** Require every PR to include a machine-generated changelog snippet in the description.

This forces contributors to explicitly state changes upfront, cutting review time by making impact obvious at a glance. The trade-off is upfront friction—engineers must run a tool or script—but it pays off by reducing back-and-forth in comments and speeding up merges. Link coverage climbs because every PR now has a clear, searchable record of what changed.

name: Scriv
text: The real risk is that requiring human-written changelogs for *every* PR—no exceptions—will slow down small fixes and discourage iterative work. A better alternative: auto-generate the changelog snippet from commit messages, then let reviewers edit it if needed. Settle it by testing both approaches for a week and measuring PR velocity and review time.
